The inverse problem is to reconstruct the shape of a perfect conductor from the electric far-field pattern of scattered time-harmonic electromagnetic waves.
The electromagnetic fields satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations in the exterior domain.
The boundary condition on the perfect conductor surface is that the tangential electric field vanishes.
The far-field pattern is an analytic tangential vector field on the unit sphere.
The problem is severely ill-posed and nonlinear, with possible non-uniqueness if only one incident field is used.
The Kirsch-Kress method approximates the scattered field by a curl potential with a tangential density on a reference surface.
Tikhonov regularization is used to stabilize the inverse problem in the Kirsch-Kress method.
The Kirsch-Kress method requires the wavenumber not to be a Maxwell eigenvalue of the reference domain.
The Colton-Monk method uses electromagnetic Herglotz wave functions and an identity relating far-field patterns to reconstruct the shape.
The Colton-Monk method introduces a fixed radiating solution to avoid the restrictive Maxwell eigenvalue condition.
The shape is parametrized as a star-like domain via a function p on the unit sphere within bounds ensuring smoothness.
The far-field pattern uniquely determines the scattered field outside the object.
Integral operators with weakly singular kernels and jump relations of potentials are key mathematical tools.
The paper proves existence of minimizers for the optimization functionals and convergence properties as regularization parameters tend to zero.
Maxwell eigenvalues correspond to frequencies where the interior Maxwell problem has nontrivial solutions, causing reconstruction difficulties.
The magnetic far-field pattern does not contain additional information beyond the electric far-field pattern.
The set of far-field patterns is not dense in the space of tangential fields if Maxwell eigenvalues exist.
The optimization methods are designed for low and resonance frequencies; for high frequencies, geometrical optics methods are preferred.
The paper provides a rigorous mathematical framework for inverse electromagnetic scattering shape reconstruction.
The methods rely on analytic continuation and compactness arguments in function spaces of tangential fields.
